findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: Attacker can inject a newline character or special characters into the input to terminate the command or inject additional commands.
findings.assumptions: The input from the user is directly used without any validation or sanitization, and it is possible that the program might execute commands based on the input.

findings.title: Buffer Overflow
findings.trigger: An attacker can send more data than the buffer can hold (258 bytes), leading to a buffer overflow.
findings.assumptions: The buffer size is fixed at 258 bytes, and there is no check to ensure that the received data does not exceed this size.

findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: If the buffer contains malicious data that is later interpreted or executed, it could lead to command injection.
findings.assumptions: The buffer is used to store and send data to the client, and there is no validation or sanitization of the data before sending.

findings.title: Buffer Overflow
findings.trigger: If the received data contains more than 258 bytes, it could lead to a buffer overflow when printed.
findings.assumptions: The buffer size is fixed at 258 bytes, and there is no check to ensure that the received data does not exceed this size when printed.
